payload.claim: The `_SENTENCE_END` regex splits a sentence boundary before a capital letter, a digit, a backtick or a quote, but every fixture in the three new witnesses only ever follows a `.!?` with a capital letter or a backtick — none starts a sentence with a bare digit. Deleting the `0-9` alternative (`r'[.!?](?=\s+[A-Z`"]|\s*$)'`) leaves all three new tests green, yet it silently changes which text two adjacent real sentences get merged into for the moved-text check whenever a spec's prose puts a plain number after a sentence-ending period (a realistic pattern in this repo's own prose style, e.g. numbered counts). The design comment above the regex explicitly claims the approximation 'never costs a false [report]', but that claim is only argued for under-splitting (merging two true sentences); the digit branch exists specifically to avoid an over-split scenario the tests never exercise, so the invariant central to acceptance criterion 3 is unverified for that branch.
